new_items.title: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission.
new_items.summary_rss: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-transmitting mosquito, has invaded Africa and rapidly adapts to the high temperatures in urban settings. However, the molecular basis of its thermal adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identified a variant of a 5-kb deletion in the circadian clock gene timeless (tim -5kb ) that rose to high frequency after 3 years of rearing at high laboratory temperatures. The tim +/ -5kb heterozygous males maintain stable expression of the period gene at high temperatures, conferring a competitive mating advantage through the increased expression of the adipokinetic hormone gene AKH1 to promote energy mobilization and flight activity, together with the upregulation of fatty acyl-CoA reductase genes FAR3 and FAR5 to enhance the production of heptacosane pheromone. Moreover, heterozygous females exhibit increased susceptibility to Plasmodium infection, increasing malaria transmission potential. These findings reveal a circadian-based genetic mechanism that may underlie thermal adaptation in An. stephensi and hold important implications for malaria control in Africa.

new_items.title: CD19 CAR T cell therapy alters disease-associated immune signatures in multiple sclerosis.
new_items.summary_rss: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory central nervous system (CNS) disease. Although current immunotherapies control relapses, they have limited impact on progression, which might reflect incomplete access to or modulation of compartmentalized CNS inflammation. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells can infiltrate tissues, but their ability to access and eliminate immune cells residing in the CNS remains elusive. We report the treatment of five individuals with progressive or relapsing-remitting MS with autologous CD19 CAR T cells to assess safety-relevant aspects, CNS bioavailability, and compartment-specific effects. The intervention induces remodeling of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) B cell pool, with a sustained reduction in CSF humoral biomarkers. Notably, CSF-infiltrating CAR T cells selectively upregulate phosphodiesterase 7B, while reconstituted peripheral B cells show altered cytokine and homing profiles. These findings indicate compartment-specific immunomodulation beyond peripheral B cell depletion and support controlled trials to test safety, durability, and efficacy.

new_items.title: Genome writing reveals SVA retrotransposon consequences in X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism.
new_items.summary_rss: Human retrotransposon insertions are often associated with diseases. Regarding neurodegenerative X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism (XDP), a human-specific SINE-VNTR-Alu (SVA) subfamily F retrotransposon was inserted in intron 32 of the TAF1 gene. Here, we genomically rewrote a portion of the mouse Taf1 allele with the corresponding 78-kb XDP patient-derived TAF1 allele. In mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs), the presence of the intronic SVA-rather than the hybrid gene structure-reduces hyTAF1 (hybrid TAF1 mRNA) levels. This leads to transcriptional downregulation of genes with TATA boxes enriched in their promoters and triggers apoptosis. Chromatin and transcriptome profiling revealed that intronic SVAs are actively transcribed, forming barriers that likely impede transcription elongation. In mice, neuronal-lineage TAF1 humanization resulted in lethality in male progeny within 2 months. XDP male mice developed severe atrophy centered on the striatum-the same brain region affected in XDP patients. Lastly, CRISPRa-mediated activation of hyTAF1 restored mESC viability, suggesting that boosting TAF1 transcription could be a therapeutic approach.

new_items.title: Genomic surveillance reveals age-structured SARS-CoV-2 transmission across settings.
new_items.summary_rss: Understanding respiratory virus transmission requires integrating pathogen genomic data with detailed epidemiological context. We analyzed >85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genomes linked to epidemiological data collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Collected in 666 settings, including schools, colleges, and skilled nursing facilities, this dataset enabled direct comparison of within-setting transmission to community-wide risk. Elevated transmission was concentrated in specific age-defined subpopulations-older adolescents in schools, undergraduates in colleges, and residents in nursing facilities-with little additional risk among other groups, notably including staff. Young adults, particularly in colleges, played a disproportionate role in spread, and new viral lineages consistently expanded first within this group. Viral spread followed reproducible urban-to-rural gradients, and vaccination was associated with reduced onward transmission. We further estimated sequencing thresholds required for timely detection of emerging variants. Together, these findings reveal consistent demographic and spatial structure in SARS-CoV-2 transmission that can inform viral respiratory pathogen genomic surveillance.

new_items.title: Myelin pathology is a key feature of X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism.
new_items.summary_rss: X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism (XDP) is an adult-onset movement disorder predominantly affecting males of Filipino descent. It is caused by the insertion of a SINE-variable number of tandem repeat (VNTR)-Alu subfamily F (SVA_F) retrotransposon in the TATA-box binding protein-associated factor 1 (TAF1) gene. A barrier to XDP research has been the lack of animal models. Here, we introduce a conditional humanized XDP mouse model harboring a hybrid mouse-human Taf1/TAF1 gene (hyTAF1) containing the pathogenic SVA_F. We activated hyTAF1 in Nestin + cells and found the resulting XDP male mice recapitulate features of human XDP, including severe motor impairment and striatal atrophy. Transcriptomic, histological, and electron microscopy analyses revealed a reduction in oligodendrocyte-lineage cells and myelin disruption. Consistent with this, postmortem brain tissue from XDP patients revealed similar myelin pathology, including loss of myelin in the medial prefrontal cortex. These results identify oligodendrocyte dysfunction and myelin loss as major contributors to XDP, providing new mechanistic insight into this disorder.

new_items.title: RNA folding drives species-dependent host mRNA partitioning in Ebola virus condensates.
new_items.summary_rss: RNA viruses form membraneless condensates in host cells to drive replication, but whether these compartments regulate host RNAs remains unclear. Using multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH)-based subcellular transcriptomics, we quantified cellular mRNA recruitment into Ebola virus condensates under basal and interferon (IFN)-stimulated states. We find that, in the basal state, cellular RNAs with minimally folded coding regions are selectively recruited. Under IFN stimulation, however, IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) with structured 3' UTRs concentrate in viral condensates. We find that both RNA structural features are conserved in the viral genome and support its retention in condensates. In parallel, for cellular mRNAs, we find that partitioning into condensates prolongs RNA half-life and amplifies, rather than dampens, ISG expression. Fruit bats, which do not experience severe disease from RNA viruses, instead have ISGs with reduced 3' UTR folding and may evade condensate sequestration, thus enabling balanced antiviral responses. This selective stabilization links condensate function to RNA regulation as a molecular determinant of virus-host co-evolution and disease pathogenesis.

Quaternary carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles.
new_items.summary_rss: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

new_items.title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects.
new_items.summary_rss: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

new_items.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme.
new_items.summary_rss: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.
